info.value:
When my husband Johnny was promoted, we were going to move again. So we put our house up for sale. Three weeks later, it was still on the market. I became a busy housekeeper. Every room had to be kept tidy, and dishes had to be washed and put away when used. Then one day the doorbell rang unexpectedly at 7:30 a.m. Sleepily, I opened the door and saw our agent Jack standing there with a couple from New York. “There had been no time to call,” he explained, “because the couple had to catch a plane home very soon.”

We had just finished breakfast. It was too late to clear up. The three people made their way past the dirty breakfast dishes on the kitchen table and into a bedroom with unmade beds. As I went into the bathroom to comb my hair, I heard the man saying something to his wife. Then they both laughed.

Two days later, the agent phoned to tell me that the couple had bought the house. He repeated what the buyer had said when he handed over the check the following day, “That house has a warm, lived-in feeling, just like ours. I like it best.”
